A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HPS research and contain 24 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content on all pages except 1 and 10; those differences are fully readable.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning and transfer experiments, human evaluations, and ablations in Section 6 and Appendix C, including Tables 2–8.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original experimental results, human evaluations, and appendix ablations in Section 6 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The HPS loss, reward-weighted sampling, and single-response sampling procedure in Section 4.2 are identical. Appendix E retains the same extension for multiple preferred responses.

E1.justification: Both versions use HH-RLHF and PKU-SafeRLHF for fine-tuning, cross-dataset transfer, and human evaluation. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments in Tables 2–5, including SFT where reported and the BT/PL variants of DPO, EXO, IPO, SPPO, and NCA.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain identical model configurations, data augmentation, metrics, training and inference settings, best-of-five response selection, and human-rating procedures.

E4.justification: The response-count ablations under fine-tuning and transfer in Tables 6–7 and the beta/KL analysis in Table 8 are unchanged. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting and run/seed disclosures are unchanged, including the existing plus-or-minus reporting for fine-tuning times in Section 6.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 2–8 and the reported training times are identical. For example, Table 3 reports the same DPO-HPS human quality score of 3.93 in both versions.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, Theorems 1–3, their Appendix B proofs, and the mathematical formulations in Appendices A and E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning hard preference sampling, computational efficiency, sample complexity, reward-margin maximization, and empirical alignment benefits.

C2.justification: Result interpretations, the limitation concerning open-source evaluation models in Section 7, and the safety and response-diversity discussion in Appendix E are identical.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the documented GitHub code location from Yqcca/HPS to LVLab-SMU/HPS. Implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any change in code contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: Related-work discussions and cited works are unchanged. The references on page 10 reflow, but their content and membership remain identical.

P1.justification: Page 10 expands the funding acknowledgement to include AcRF Tier 2 support, another Tier 1 grant, and a funder disclaimer. Apart from the code address and version stamp, the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgement shifts the Impact Statement and references on page 10, moving the start of the Chiang reference into the right column. The first-page version stamp changes; Figure 1 and Tables 1–8 retain identical displays.

improvement.justification: v4 updates the repository pointer and expands funding disclosures while retaining identical methods, empirical evidence, proofs, limitations, and scientific exposition. These limited documentation and layout updates establish no meaningful net change in overall paper quality; improved code accessibility cannot be inferred from the address change.
